HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Misc(Pet.) No. 3040/2023 1.

Mukesh Pareek S/o Sh. Hanuman Sahay Pareek, Aged  About 52 Years, B/c Brahmin, R/o 133, Krishnam,
 Jagatpura, Airport Turminal, Police Station Jawahar Circle,
 Jaipur (Raj.)

2. Hanuman Sahay Pareek S/o Late Sh. Uma Shankar, Aged  About 72 Years, B/c Brahmin, R/o 133, Krishnam,
 Jagatpura, Airport Turminal, Police Station Jawahar Circle,
 Jaipur (Raj.)
 ----Petitioners  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Smt. Monika Mathur D/o Sh. Amrat Lal Mathur, B/c  Mathur, Presently R/o H-111, U.i.t. Colony, Pratap Nagar,
 Jodhpur (Raj.)
 ----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. C.S. Rathore

For Respondent(s) : Ms. Anita Gehlot, PP  Mr. D.S. Baghela  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR GARG Order 01/06/2023 The instant criminal misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioners for quashing the order dated 10.05.2023 passed by Special Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (PCPNDT Act) Cases, Jodhpur Metropolitan, Jodhpur in Regular Criminal Case No.36/2017 arising out of FIR No.150/2016 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana (West),
District Jodhpur and all consequential proceedings for offences under Section 498- A of IPC on the basis of compromise entered between the parties.
(2 of 2) [CRLMP-3040/2023

] Counsel for the parties submit that they have entered into a compromise in the spirit of Lok Adalat and settled their dispute amicably, therefore, the criminal proceedings offence under Section 498-A IPC may be quashed on the basis of compromise.

Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case, since the petitioner and complainant have arrived at compromise and settled their dispute and in the view of the law laid down by the Mukesh Pareek vs State Of Rajasthan on 1 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43106186/

sentences.text: Hon'ble Apex court in the case of B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana, reported in 2003 (4) SCC p.675 in which it has been held that the proceedings under Section 498A IPC can be quashed because it is the matrimonial matter, the criminal proceedings for offence under Section 498-A IPC are liable to be quashed.

entities.text: B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana, reported in 2003 (4) SCC p.675

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the present misc. petition is allowed qua the petitioners and order dated 10.05.2023 passed by Special Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (PCPNDT Act) Cases, Jodhpur Metropolitan,
Jodhpur in Regular Criminal Case No.36/2017 arising out of FIR No.150/2016 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana (West), District Jodhpur and all consequential proceedings for offences under Section 498-A of IPC are hereby quashed on the basis of compromise deed.
Stay petition also stands disposed of.
(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 322-/rashi/-
